analytical_question: Can NYU design, staff and govern a short, supervised stockroom comparison, and what evidence would justify starting and subsequently closing that trial?
general_et_finding: The dossier documents humanoid work in bounded industrial programs. An organization considering another setting needs evidence about its particular human tasks, equipment and response arrangements. The industrial examples establish neither typical supervision demand nor the reliability of a candidate robot on a campus.
application_finding: The proposed test isolates pickup, travel and placement on either of two low shelves along one restricted, single-floor route. A supervisor has to recognize an unsafe placement or entry, stop work and arrange recovery. The cart baseline captures the whole task. A wheeled option with human handoff, if feasible, isolates the possible value of robot shelf placement. Safe placement, intervention burden and the viability of all handoffs remain empirical questions.
organization_specific_finding: At the 2026-11-17 cutoff, C1 describes a hypothetical experiment. The roles below are proposed evidence owners. | Leadership/sponsorship — Unknown, high. The case defines a cautious scope, but sponsor commitment, site permission and approval rights are unverified. Campus leadership and the operations manager would identify the decision maker before resources are committed. | Skills/training — Unknown, critical. Operator availability and demonstrated ability to recognize unsafe motion or a marginal placement, stop, correct or escalate, and recover are separately unverified. A missed cue could expose a worker to contact. The operations manager would roster personnel and the EHS reviewer would witness a representative competence exercise. | Process/workflow — Partial, high. C1 specifies a route, two destinations and manual fallback. There is no verified local procedure for checking tote condition, clearing the route, accepting placement, recording exceptions and handing back to cart work. A premature handoff could expose workers to a falling tote. Proposed owner: stockroom operations manager. | Infrastructure/data — Unknown, high. Site geometry, egress, accessible passage, tote/shelf fit, equipment availability, access boundary and camera/log settings need local inspection. An unsuitable route or recording configuration could compromise access or privacy. Facilities and IT/privacy would review the site and data flow respectively. | Resources/budget — Unknown, high. Procurement access, insurance terms, pilot funds and protected supervision, review and recovery time are unverified. A short-staffed shift could leave the route unsupervised. Operations and procurement would establish coverage and full trial cost; recurring capacity needs a separate decision. | Governance/risk — Unknown, critical. An emergency stop and boundary are proposed. Site-specific hazard review, stop verification, risk acceptance, privacy disposition and incident response remain unverified. Approval without them could allow uncontrolled motion or unauthorized recording. Proposed reviewers: EHS and IT/privacy, with management accepting residual risk. | Culture/change — Unknown, moderate. Staff are identified as affected stakeholders, but consultation, workload feedback, reporting arrangements and willingness to challenge unsafe work are unverified. Unreported near misses would distort the comparison. Stockroom workers and their manager would design the feedback route. | Operating ownership — Unknown, critical and dominant. No evidence identifies a person delegated to stop the trial, a backup for incidents or who authorizes restart. A supervisor might recognize entry into the route yet wait for permission while the robot continues moving. The operations manager would secure written delegation and backup coverage for each trial period. C1 establishes uncertainty about authority, not that authority was refused.

evidence.claim: A specific industrial logistics pilot led to a commercial agreement.
GXO reported continuation of the program and plans for additional sites.
evidence.notes: Additional 2027 sites were plans at cutoff.

evidence.claim: BMW reported bounded humanoid use in its plants.
evidence.evidence_type: Company press release in supplied dossier
evidence.notes: Provides no independent campus performance or staffing measure.

evidence.claim: Risk assessment, guarding and training are relevant review topics.
evidence.source_or_reference: R4, OSHA Industrial Robots and Robot System Safety
evidence.evidence_type: Government guidance summarized in supplied dossier
evidence.notes: EHS must verify current scope and applicability before relying on guidance for a site decision.

evidence.claim: The specified comparison and its controls are proposals; no local implementation, clearance or staffing is verified.
evidence.source_or_reference: C1, team-proposed NYU stockroom use case
evidence.notes: The readiness profile and gates are specialist inferences, not NYU findings.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Industrial precedent supports investigating fit. It supplies no site-specific evidence of floor clearance, load stability, operator response or comparative labor cost.
The lack of verified permissions, funds or staff does not establish a denial or failed exercise. No representative trial results or recurring resource commitments are supplied.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that the packet cannot support powered-trial authorization. Confidence in NYU's actual capabilities, candidate performance and supervision cost is low because the packet contains no site measurements, signed decisions or witnessed trials.
value_opportunity_implication: Count stable placements and total worker minutes per accepted placement, including handoff, supervision, interventions and recovery. Record cart results under the same route, tote and shelf conditions. Document any reason a wheeled comparison cannot be run, and limit comparative conclusions accordingly.
risk_governance_implication: Give the on-duty supervisor and backup a clear stop pathway, keep workers outside the approved boundary, and route safety, privacy and purchasing decisions to EHS, IT/privacy and procurement. The responsible NYU decision maker would approve scope and residual risk in writing before any powered stockroom test.
recommendation_management_implication: REQUEST EVIDENCE — discovery and design of the bounded comparison can proceed on paper; withhold authorization for a powered proof of concept. 1. P0 stage gate: stop and incident ownership are unverified. Before commissioning equipment, the proposed operations manager obtains signed site sponsorship, named stop delegation, backup coverage, escalation and restart rights. These unlock detailed site planning. 2. P0 stage gate: route, equipment, data use and costs are unverified. Before committing to test dates, proposed Facilities, EHS, IT/privacy and procurement reviewers document route and shelf fit, access/egress, permitted recording, provider conditions and insurance, quotes and funded staff hours. Signed dispositions unlock preparation of an approved rehearsal. 3. P0 stage gate: procedure and competence are unverified. Before powered stockroom use, proposed operations and EHS leads document a roster, safe simulated error-seeded drills, detection and response times, verified stop function in an approved environment, cart fallback, coverage and sign-off against pre-agreed criteria. With management risk acceptance these unlock a decision on this short supervised trial only. 4. P1 pilot learning: comparative performance is unknown. At the agreed end of the test the proposed operations manager reviews time, accepted placements, interventions, incidents, staff feedback and full costs against criteria agreed before entry. This unlocks closure, rejection or a new scoped request; any scale decision requires separate recurring staffing, funding and control evidence.
change_monitoring_triggers: During an authorized trial, the designated supervisor pauses immediately on unexpected motion, a boundary breach, unstable tote, unreliable stop, missing supervisor or unexpected recording. Secure the area, invoke the approved incident procedure, and return to cart work only after the area is safe. Resume only with documented clearance from the designated restart authority.

Operations logs every run and exception and reviews near misses, workload and throughput at each session close. Repeated interventions, failed placement criteria or unacceptable supervision time trigger suspension and review against management-adopted limits.

Changes to equipment, software, route, shelf, tote, staff, camera settings, support or insurance terms reopen the affected gate before further testing. Date every refresh. At the agreed end date, stop testing and review the complete comparator record.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Who may stop, manage an incident and authorize restart on each shift? The site sponsor and operations manager should supply named delegations, backups and coverage before pilot authorization.

Which exact route, tote, shelves, equipment and data settings are acceptable? Facilities, EHS, IT/privacy and procurement should supply the site assessment, approved configuration, privacy decision, insurance and vendor terms before committing to the trial.

Who can staff each role, and what proves they can perform it? Operations should provide funded rostered time. EHS should provide observed exercise results for detection, correction, escalation, recovery and elapsed response time, plus stop verification, before powered testing.

What criteria will end the test and what did workers experience? Operations and affected staff should provide the agreed protocol, comparator feasibility and feedback process before entry, then results and incidents at exit. Any future operating proposal also needs an accountable service owner, recurring budget and staff coverage.
